study type: Retrospective cohort study using machine learning for prediction
exposure: Clinical risk factors for postpartum hemorrhage (e.g., hematocrit, shock index, white blood cell count, gestational hypertension, BMI, total amniotic fluid, time of second labor, neonatal weight)
Features of uterine contraction curves (e.g., frequency of contractions, mean area of contractions)
cohort: The study included 10,520 women who had vaginal deliveries with complete study data at the First Hospital of Jinan University between 2016 and 2020.
finding: Machine learning models, particularly LGB+LR incorporating uterine contraction features and clinical risk factors, significantly improved the accuracy of predicting postpartum hemorrhage after vaginal delivery.
mod_finding: The study specifically focused on improving postpartum hemorrhage prediction for women undergoing vaginal delivery.
followup_time: Observations for postpartum hemorrhage were taken primarily within 2 hours after vaginal delivery.
birth_weight: Neonatal weight (kg) was identified as one of the important predictors for severe postpartum hemorrhage, but specific weights of the cohort are not provided.
gest_age: Gestational hypertension was identified as one of the important predictors for severe postpartum hemorrhage, but specific gestational ages of the cohort are not provided.
